title: The Mainspring
summary: Something on Trinity Street is ticking, and it is not a clock. Pip Hobbe follows the Unwinder's oil north, to a watchmaker's shop that should not be open at this hour.

intro.line: Four bells of twelve sleep easy again. Up the hill, past the Senate House, something keeps a beat that no clock in Cambridge was built to keep.

steps.text: Ask Pip Hobbe where the ticking is coming from

travel.caption: Pip leads you up past the Senate House, nose to the gutter, onto Trinity Street

dialogue.line: Hear it, Late'un? Tick. Tick. Up the hill. Pip's ears hurt with it.
Corvin's oil again?
Oil and brass filings, all up Trinity Street. Come on. Stay close. Hobs don't like clockmakers. They count things.

steps.text: Follow Pip's nose up Trinity Street

intro.line: Brass filings glitter in the gutter like spilt sugar. They lead uphill, towards one lit window.

dialogue.line: There. The clock shop. Lamp's lit, sign says shut. Somebody's lying, and it ain't the sign.

steps.text: Confront the clockmaker, Tamsin Ashdown, outside her workshop

intro.line: A young woman in a leather apron is locking the shop door from the outside. Her hands are black with oil.

dialogue.line: We're closed. Repairs by appointment. Goodnight.
Your hands are covered in the same oil that put four bell-guardians to sleep.

choices.text: Your hands are covered in his oil.

reply.line: Half the clocks in Cambridge run on that oil. It proves nothing.
He's my uncle. That isn't a crime. Not yet.

dialogue.line: Fine. He came to me a month ago. He wanted a key cut to a pattern no locksmith would touch. I cut it. I didn't ask.
Behind my back wall there is a ward-clock, the Mainspring. It keeps the street's hour. Tonight he's been in there, and it's running down.
Listen. Hear that? The bicycles are moving.

steps.text: Stop the Bicycle-Golems and Clockwork Porters assembling on Trinity Street

intro.line: Up and down Trinity Street the parked bicycles shake off their locks. Moss crawls up the frames and stands them on their back wheels.
Behind them two brass porters wind themselves up out of a shop doorway, keys turning in their backs.

dialogue.line: Those porters are my uncle's work. I'd know his rivets anywhere. He's winding the whole street against us.
The Mainspring's door is in the wall up by the Great Gate. Go. I'll follow when my hands stop shaking.

steps.text: Find the Mainspring's hidden door near the Great Gate

intro.line: The taper in your hand flares. A door that was not there a moment ago outlines itself in the old brick, ticking.

dialogue.line: Inside, a clock without a face: a great coiled spring of black steel, nearly slack. Each tick comes slower than the last.
Someone is standing in front of the gate, waiting for you.

steps.text: Face the man waiting by the Great Gate

intro.line: A grey-haired man in a long dark coat, keys at his belt, oil on his cuffs. He looks tired rather than wicked.

dialogue.line: You must be the Latecomer. The one who keeps waking things I put to sleep. Go home.
You're unwinding the city's guardians, Corvin. Why?

reply.line: Because twelve bells were never the whole oath. Someone scraped out the thirteenth. I mean to read it.

choices.text: Your niece is ashamed of you.

reply.line: Tamsin will understand. She always takes a thing apart before she judges it.

dialogue.line: The Mainspring is unwound. What's left is its guardian, and it does not know me any more. It will not know you either.
He steps back into the shadow of the gate, turns a key in nothing, and is gone. Something behind the wall begins to tick very loudly.

steps.text: Defeat the Escapement Engine before the Great Gate

intro.line: The wall opens like a clock case. Out of it walks a thing of brass and oak the height of a shop-front, an escapement wheel turning in its chest.
It moves on the beat. Every blow lands on the tick. Learn the beat, and you can step between them.

dialogue.line: The escapement wheel jams on a broken tooth. The Engine stops mid-stride, sighs out a breath of hot oil, and sits down on the setts like a tired porter.
Behind you, a lamp swings up the street. Tamsin, running.

steps.text: Help Tamsin decide what to do with the Mainspring

dialogue.line: He was here, wasn't he. He left you to be ticked to death by his own guardian.
I can rewind the Mainspring. It'll take me all night, and he'll know it was me.
Then he'll know whose side you're on.

choices.text: Then he'll know whose side you're on.
You don't have to choose tonight.

reply.line: I do, though. That's the thing about clocks. They don't wait for you.

dialogue.line: Take my loupe. It finds the weak tooth in anything that ticks. You'll need it more than I will.
And listen. He always said the conduit was the weak stitch. The water. He's going for Hobson's Conduit next.
